log.text: Your net worth fell by $16K this year. Change in home value −$13K · Interest on debt −$2,787 · Shortfall in living costs −$1,103 · Debt paid down by cutting back +$1,323
You had no money, but you lent a hand at a neighbor's funeral.
Riley, who has a home of their own now, called to see how you were.
On a quiet morning with nothing to do, a warm cup of tea felt especially good.
You heard that Noah had become a team leader at work.

You hadn't eaten properly for days. At a supermarket you put bread and milk in your bag. A clerk caught you, but the owner heard you out, took only the price and let you go without calling the police. You lowered your head every time you passed that shop.
The neighbor you used to bicker with over small things now asks how you are.
Your younger sister died at 74. (Pancreatitis)
Age 80. Of the girls born in Canada the same year as you, about 74% are still alive.
You spent time with your grandchild.
You told your grandchild stories about Calgary, where you were born.
Your family gathered for your eightieth birthday. In the photo of everyone together, you were right in the middle.
With your hiking group you reached the top of a famous mountain.
You had a big fight with your older brother and made up a few months later.
You had a routine health checkup. Nothing was wrong.
Voices grew hard to make out, and you often had to ask people to repeat themselves. You held off on hearing aids for now and followed people by watching their lips.
log.fact: Moderate or worse hearing loss affects 12.7% of people at 60 and over 58% at 90. Of those a hearing aid would help, only about 17% use one (WHO World Report on Hearing 2021)

Riley got married. You gave what you could.
You were diagnosed with angina. As before, you made sure to take your medicine.
Liam's daughter started school. You bought a school bag.
